name: Open type-dimension statements
licence: Written for this app and released into the public domain (CC0). Not adapted from the MBTI, 16Personalities or any other published type test.
scale: Same five answers as the main test: 1 = Not me at all … 5 = Very much me.
design: Twelve statements per dimension, six pointing at each pole, so that agreeing with everything cancels out. Each describes one concrete situation. Both poles are worded as equally reasonable ways to be, so the statements measure preference rather than how nice, clever or hard-working someone is.

items.text: After a long week, seeing friends gives me more energy than a quiet night in.
After a day full of people, I need time alone before I feel like myself again.
I work out what I think by talking it through with someone.
I prefer to think something through fully before I say it out loud.
In a new group, I usually speak to people first rather than wait to be spoken to.
I would rather have one long conversation with one person than short chats with ten.
A busy shared space suits me better than working alone in a quiet room.
I do my best work when I can shut the door and not be interrupted.
On a long journey, I would rather chat with the person next to me than put my headphones in.
A free weekend with no plans and no people sounds like a treat.
I like having a wide circle of friends and something on most evenings.
In a class or meeting, I often have a view but keep it to myself unless I am asked.
When I learn something new, I want real examples first and the theory second.
I enjoy thinking about questions that have no practical use.
I trust what has worked before more than an untested new idea.
I am more interested in what something could become than in what it is now.
When I give directions, I list the exact steps and landmarks.
In a conversation, I often jump to a connected idea before the first one is finished.
I notice and remember practical details that others miss, like prices, dates and who said what.
When I look at a problem, I see the overall pattern before I see the details.
I would rather fix a real problem in front of me than discuss what might happen in ten years.
I get bored doing a task the same way twice and look for a new way to do it.
When I read instructions, I follow them in order rather than work it out my own way.
I often read between the lines and look for what a person really means.
When a friend brings me a problem, my first instinct is to help fix it rather than to comfort them.
Before I decide something, I think first about how it will affect the people involved.
In a disagreement, getting it right matters more to me than keeping everyone comfortable.
When two people argue, I want to help each see the other's side more than I want to work out who is right.
When I make a hard decision, I weigh the pros and cons and go with the logic, even if it feels harsh.
A decision can make perfect sense on paper and still be wrong if it goes against my values.
I think the same rule should apply to everyone, even when someone has a sad story.
I would bend a rule if following it would hurt someone who did nothing wrong.
I would rather be told an uncomfortable truth plainly than have it softened.
When I give feedback, I think carefully about how the person will take it before I speak.
When I judge a piece of work, I look at the result and not at how hard the person tried.
I find it hard to feel good about a sensible decision if it upsets someone I care about.
I like to have a decision made and settled rather than left open.
I like to keep my options open for as long as I can before I commit.
Before a trip, I plan where I will be each day.
I am happy to set off for a day out with no plan and see what happens.
I feel uneasy until a task is finished, so I do the work first and relax after.
I do my best work in a burst close to the deadline.
I keep a list or a calendar and feel unsettled when plans change at short notice.
When plans change at the last minute, I find it easy to adapt and often enjoy it.
I like my day to follow a routine I have set out.
I see rules and timetables as a rough guide rather than something to stick to.
When I shop for something big, I decide what I want, buy it and stop looking.
I enjoy starting new things more than finishing them.
